A puffin stands bolt upright at the very edge of the ground, smaller than the clump of pink flowers beside it, looking entirely unbothered.
Three puffins in a row on one flat slab all face the same way the wind is going, the slab twice as long as all three of them together.
A big white-and-grey gull stands into the wind on a bare table of rock, its feathers blown flat and hard against its body.
A line of white seabirds glides past below the level of the ground, the picture looking straight down onto their bright backs.
A big white seabird hangs dead still in the wind at the edge where the ground stops, neither rising nor moving forward at all.
A glossy black crow with a curved bright red beak walks through the pink flowers over bare rock, turning small stones over.
A falcon stands on a slab barely broader than the flower clump beside it, the wind combing its back feathers up the wrong way in pale raked lines.
Grey seals are hauled out on flat wet rock far below, small and slug-shaped with distance, a dozen pale smears on dark stone.
A rabbit sits up in grass it has cropped to almost nothing, the pink flowers surviving only at the reach it cannot quite manage.
A stoat is half out of the gap between two stones, its long body bent around the corner of the lower rock.
A small brown bird sings from the very top of a gorse bush while the whole bush is bent hard inland under a sky the colour of tin.
Twenty or more small pale-blue butterflies work one clump of pink flowers, their wings opening and closing like slow blinking.
A dozen or more bumblebees work low over the flowers, each one blown sideways and coming stubbornly back.
A raven stands on bare rock with the wind lifting its throat feathers into a rough grey beard it did not arrive with.
A puffin stands in the flowers at the very edge of a crack in the rock, its orange feet planted on either side of the gap.
A big white-and-grey gull stands on a boulder sitting in grass, leaning forward into the wind, yellow-beaked and furious.
A glossy black crow with red legs picks its way across loose broken stone, the pink flowers threading up between the rocks around it.
A falcon sits on a knob of bare rock, smaller than the rock is wide, its dark hood turned hard into the wind.
A rabbit crouches flat in a dip in the ground, its ears pressed back, flowers bent above it on three sides.
A stoat is out on bare open rock between two clumps of flowers, low and liquid and moving fast toward the nearest shadow.
Twenty or more small copper-orange butterflies cover one clump of flowers, barely one wing-width between them.
A puffin stands at the edge of a crack in the rock looking straight down into it, its big bright beak almost touching the rock.
A dozen or more bumblebees are blown off the flowers in one gust and hang scattered in the air above the bare rock before descending.
Three grey seals hauled out below are so small with distance they read at first as pale oval stones, until one of them moves.
A small brown bird sings from the top of a gorse bush at the very edge of the ground with open water a long way down behind it.
